text:
Lina Gomez: Quick sync - Vertex Health renewal is yellow. CS wants a one-pager customers can follow to cut token spend and reduce latency before the next billing cycle. Keep it non-invasive (no infra changes).
Ben Harper: Good candidate for client-side fixes: response caching, delta-batching, and stream fallbacks. short and prescriptive.
Surya Iyer: For cache: recommend stateless key pattern: "app_session:v2:<stable_user_hash>:template_id". avoid raw PII; use a reversible hash only if they manage keys. TTL suggestions depend on cadence: 12h for chatbots with multiple daily interactions, 48h for weekly workflows.
Cass W.: Add guidance to never cache responses that include ephemeral tokens or PHI. include a simple opt-out header: `X-Redwood-Cache: no-store`.
Lina Gomez: Add two ready-to-paste snippets (Go + Node) and a tiny delta-batch pseudocode. Keep each snippet <= 8 lines.
Ben Harper: Node snippet:
```js
// Node: session key + cache
const key = `app_session:v2:${sha256(userId)}:${templateId}`
if (cache.get(key)) return cache.get(key)
const res = await redwood.generate(req)
cache.set(key, res, {ttl: 3600})
```
Surya Iyer: Go snippet (pseudo):
```go
// Go: delta batch helper
batch := make([]Turn,0)
for _, turn := range turns {
  if turn.IsNew { batch = append(batch, turn) }
}
resp := client.Generate(batch)
```
Lina Gomez: Delta batching rules: 1) send only appended turns, 2) cap re-sent history to last N tokens (e.g., 512), 3) if any turn is labeled `safety=true` do full-history send.
Cass W.: Batch window guidance: prefer event-driven batching (flush on N=8 OR T=200ms). For low TPS, use immediate send. Document both knobs.
Ben Harper: Streaming fallback pattern: attempt SSE/ws stream with chunk SLO=1s. If average chunk latency > 1.5s or total > 6s, switch to: async job + progress webhook + short polling (5s). Provide UX guidance: show spinner + partial text if stream fails.
Surya Iyer: Telemetry: paste these events for customers to hook into their analytics: `redwood.cache.hit`, `redwood.cache.miss`, `redwood.delta.batch.size`, `redwood.stream.aborted`. Include dimensions: session_id, model, tokens_sent, reason_code.
Lina Gomez: KPIs to measure pre/post: median latency, p50 token spend per session, cache hit rate, % sessions with aborted stream, average batch size. Aim for 20-30% token reduction first 2 weeks.
Cass W.: Troubleshooting cheats (short table lines):
- repeated/wrong answer -> likely cache too coarse; increase key granularity
- high token spend after batching -> check if safety flag forces full history
- streaming stalls -> check chunk SLO and network packet loss
Lina Gomez: CSM coach script (one paragraph):
"This one-pager focuses on three changes you can apply today: light-weight session response caching, delta-batching only new turns, and a graceful stream fallback. We'll measure success using median latency and token spend per session. If you see regressions, revert cache or disable batching for flagged flows while we triage."
Ben Harper: Rollout checklist (bulletized in the doc): add backup toggle, telemetry enabled, QA on staging with synthetic sessions, 48h watch window.
Surya Iyer: Small note for legal/compliance teams: include a checkbox in the doc to confirm PHI/PII is not being persisted; give customers the exact header to disable caching.
enablement-bot: Customer record: "Vertex Health" (vh-acct-32). renewal_status: "watchlist". playbook_id: "cs-mini-cache-batch-2026"
Lina Gomez: Timeline: I'll assemble the one-pager + snippets today and drop into the account playbook; Ben will review tonight; Surya will prepare telemetry JSON for their dashboard.
Cass W.: I'll add a short GIF showing a streaming fallback UX example to the doc after review.
Ben Harper: tagging onboarding lead @Surya for telemetry ownership. :rocket:
Lina Gomez: thanks everyone — will post the final PDF here when ready.
